static: every APPLY/ROLLBACK pack = ONE BEGIN, SET LOCAL lock_timeout 5s then advisory lock 2979301232487107403 then SET LOCAL lock_timeout 5s as the exact statements 2-4 after it (tightened from: lock is statement 2), one COMMIT last, drift guard, no data DML, no secrets
generator is reproducible: build.mjs --check is clean (packs == inputs)
replica sanity: the installed ORIGINAL functions equal the captured prod text (pg_get_functiondef == facts) and DRIFT_QUERY/POSTCHECKS(S0) read S0_original
APPLY-01 on the original: succeeds, retained SELECT all ok, state S1, POSTCHECKS(S1) ok; check_in_ticket still original
APPLY-02 after 01: succeeds, state S2, POSTCHECKS(S2) ok
apply order is enforced: APPLY-02 on the original (core absent) refuses with DRIFT and changes nothing
second run refuses cleanly: APPLY-01 twice and APPLY-02 twice (DRIFT, nothing changed)
drift guard aborts APPLY-01 when: scan body altered (comment appended)
drift guard aborts APPLY-01 when: scan ACL changed (anon granted)

drift guard aborts APPLY-01 when: schema private already exists

drift guard aborts APPLY-01 when: event_orders policy added

drift guard aborts APPLY-01 when: event_orders table ACL narrowed (TRUNCATE revoked from anon)
drift guard aborts APPLY-01 when: event_orders CHECK changed (extra status value)
drift guard aborts APPLY-01 when: event_orders trigger added
drift guard aborts APPLY-01 when: event_orders UNIQUE constraint added
drift guard aborts APPLY-01 when run by a role other than postgres
drift guard aborts APPLY-02 when check_in_ticket body drifted (after step 1)
drift guard aborts APPLY-02 when the core was tampered with
ROLLBACK restores the captured originals EXACTLY: byte-identical pg_get_functiondef and prosrc, equal sorted ACL, config, owner; private schema and core gone; data untouched
rollback order is enforced and rollback has its own drift guard
advisory lock serialises two runs: B waits on the advisory lock while A holds the transaction open, then B refuses cleanly (DRIFT); end state S1
lock is shared across packs: a concurrent ROLLBACK/APPLY of a different pack also queues (same key)

TIMEOUT (lock_timeout follow-up): A (real APPLY-01) holds the pack lock ~7 s; B (the same pack) waits on the advisory lock and fails with SQLSTATE 55P03 lock_not_available after ~5 s (4.5-6.5 s), not after A's ~7 s; A is unaffected (commits, state S1); B changed nothing and holds no advisory lock afterwards

NEGATIVE CONTROL for P14: the same APPLY-01 with the PRE-lock lock_timeout removed (timeout only after the lock, the literal 'after the lock' placement) is NOT bounded: B waits out A's whole ~7 s hold and then refuses with DRIFT (not 55P03)
